subject: Post-call: token-rate delta validation + next steps (QuickShip)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Jon Lee <jon@quickship.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: throughput & streaming requirements (QuickShip)

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned. Good summary attached (qs_workload_sample.csv).

Key points we captured from the discovery:
- Primary path: conversational checkout (streaming, 1:1 agent-like sessions).
- SLA target you asked for: 95th pct request latency <= 200 ms for streaming first-byte and tail for short responses.
- Expected baseline traffic: 200 QPS sustained (steady-state) translating to ~14k tokens/sec baseline across the fleet.
- Peak profile: 2x to 8x cresting behavior during promotional spikes — peaks to 1,600 QPS for ~10-20 minute windows; token spikes to ~110k tokens/sec on crest.
- Typical message shape: median response ~75 tokens, median user turn ~30 tokens; 60% of sessions are multi-turn (avg 4 turns).
- Concurrency: target concurrent streaming sessions ~2,000 active streams during peak crest.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Jon/QA: send a representative payload sample + CSV with time series of QPS and tokens over 7 days (we got the initial file; please confirm it contains crest events).
2) Redwood (Aditya/Camila): produce a sizing note (tokens/sec vs QPS conversion, GPU slot estimate for dedicated vs hosted fallback plan) and a short canary run plan.
3) Align on latency SLO headroom tradeoffs (e.g., 95th vs 99th) and acceptable degradation modes (e.g., fallback to smaller model or lower streaming chunk rate).

Attachments: qs_workload_sample.csv (sample time series), suggested agenda for a 30-min follow-up test window next week.

Thanks — I’ll draft preliminary sizing and options by tomorrow EOD and include a quick cost delta for reserved capacity vs on-demand.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jon Lee <jon@quickship.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput & streaming requirements (QuickShip)

Thanks Aditya — confirming and added a few clarifications. Attaching fuller telemetry export (qs_workload_sample.csv) and a small summary table in the body.

Quick clarifications:
- The 1,600 QPS crest is correct but generally happens in 2–3 ten-minute bursts per promo day; otherwise cresting is 3–5x.
- Avg response sizes: we saw a bimodal distribution; ~70% of responses are short (<=80 tokens), the rest are long form (200–800 tokens) when the assistant returns a templated shipment summary.
- Concurrent streams: 2,000 is a planning target; internal ops can tolerate graceful degradation (we care most about first-byte latency for streaming UX).

Attached: qs_workload_sample.csv (time series with per-minute QPS and tokens).

We’re happy to run a test window next Wed (2026-12-09) 09:00–10:30 PST if that works for you — we can route a portion of traffic to your canary. Also want a rough estimate of cost uplift for reserved capacity sized for crest vs steady.

— Jon
Jon Lee
VP Product, QuickShip
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Jon Lee <jon@quickship.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput & streaming requirements (QuickShip)

Appreciate the quick follow — I reviewed the export and sketched an initial sizing and risk matrix. Putting the highlights inline so we can iterate quickly. Full sizing PDF will follow this afternoon.

Assumptions we used to map tokens <-> capacity:
- Baseline conversion: 1 GPU slot (A100-sized equivalent served in Redwood Dedicated) supports ~25k tokens/sec for typical chatting workloads with streaming enabled and KV caching for repeated context (50–70 token response avg).
- For mixed response shapes (short + long templates), we model token-weighted capacity; long-form templated replies increase token/sec by ~3x per QPS for those requests.

Preliminary capacity bands (rounded):
- Steady-state (200 QPS, ~14k tokens/sec): 1 slot baseline (headroom 1.5x).
- Moderate crest (600 QPS, ~42k tokens/sec): 2 slots recommended with autoscale thresholds.
- Full crest (1,600 QPS, ~110k tokens/sec): 5 slots to keep 95th latency near target; consider 6 for 99th latency buffer.

Operational mitigations to reduce cost while preserving UX:
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated lookups (reduce token count for templated parts).
- Burst capacity policy: reserved steady pool + short-duration burst pool with rapid warm-up models (quantized variants).
- Streaming chunk tuning: smaller chunk size reduces time-to-first-byte but increases per-token opcount; we can tune for first-byte priority.

Canary plan (outline):
1) Day -1: smoke test on test cluster (10m sustained at 1.5x baseline).
2) Day 0: route 5% of production traffic during planned promo time window; monitor 95th/99th latencies, token drop-rate, and concurrency health.
3) If pass: ramp to 20% and then 50% over 2 hours. If failures: automatic fallback to smaller model (same checkpoint quantized) and abort ramp.

Action items:
- Jon: confirm the test window (you proposed 2026-12-09 09:00–10:30 PST).
- QuickShip infra: share any guardrails (max concurrent connections per IP, socket limits) we should respect.
- Redwood: we’ll send a draft SLA appendix showing modeled latency buckets and cost deltas for reserved capacity vs on-demand by EOD today.

FYI CC Marissa for pricing and Camila for runbook/ops.

— Aditya
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Jon Lee <jon@quickship.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput & streaming requirements (QuickShip)

Couple of operational notes from the console/ops side before the canary:
- Telemetry: we’ll want token-level traces for first-byte and tail latency (we’ll provide a small client SDK snippet to emit spans). Please confirm you can accept an extra header for trace id injection.
- Alerts: propose alert thresholds for 95th latency > 250ms or token drop-rate > 0.5% over a 5min window.
- Rollback triggers: sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 85% for more than 3 min or error rate > 1%.

Runbook items we’ll prepare and share:
1) Run window playbook with checklists (smoke, canary, ramp, rollback).
2) Required firewall entries and IP allowlist for our canary hosts.
3) Minimal data retention and log forwarding config for your compliance team.

Also flagging that long-form templated responses are the biggest risk to token surge; if you can pre-generate or cache templates server-side for >30% of those responses we can shave peak token/sec materially.

I’ll drop the runbook draft into the shared Drive link and copy you both.

— Camila
From: Jon Lee <jon@quickship.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, QA Team <infra@quickship.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput & streaming requirements (QuickShip)

Thanks team — this is helpful. Confirming the 2026-12-09 09:00–10:30 PST test window. QA will provision traffic slices and share a short test-plan doc.

Two quick asks before the run:
1) Cost delta: please send a (ballpark) monthly cost delta for keeping reserved capacity at 5 slots (handles full crest per your note) vs a hybrid: reserved 2 slots + burst on-demand.
2) Can you propose a short latency SLA appendix we can share with procurement? We’re aiming to keep contractual 95th under 250ms for streaming first-byte, with credits for larger outages.

We’ll also push a small patch to avoid server-side template expansion for 40% of traffic (should reduce peak tokens).

Appreciate the partnership — we’ll review the runbook once you drop it and confirm firewall IPs.

— Jon
